Sources indicate that tired of Wi-Fi drops throughout your home? The best mesh Wi-Fi systems can eliminate internet dead zones and turn your house into a powerhouse for connectivity, no matter how far away devices are from a router. To prove it, we've done the testing to help you find the right mesh system.

At Tom's Guide, we put each mesh Wi-Fi system through real-world scenarios, from multi-story homes to outdoor use. This allows us to see how fast internet speeds are at multiple ranges, especially through objects and walls. So, if you've been struggling to get a strong Wi-Fi signal across your home, the mesh Wi-Fi systems we recommend will help you sort that problem out.

For the best mesh Wi-Fi system you can buy today, we recommend the MSI Roami BE Pro for reliable speeds and long-distance coverage. This Wi-Fi 7 mesh system will take you far for its price, but there are more options we've tested for homes.

It has been revealed that soon, you'll see more of the next standard of mesh Wi-Fi systems arrive with Wi-Fi 8. We've already tested the first Wi-Fi 8 router, but there's no need to rush to get this yet, as there aren't any consumer devices that can take advantage of it. In the meantime, we have even more mesh systems worth considering!

According to recent reports, for the latest wireless connectivity, or to cover your home on a budget, this guide will help you find the best mesh Wi-Fi system for your needs, with in-depth reviews and test results. Let's dive in.

It has been revealed that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The MSI Roamii BE Pro isn't the fastest around, nor does it deliver the longest range, but it excels at speeds, distances and setup for half the price of other tri-band WiFi 7 routers. That's why it's the best mesh Wi-Fi system we recommend for most, especially if you're looking for an affordable way to upgrade to Wi-Fi 7.

Sources indicate that the Roamii BE Pro immediately stands out for its real-world speed across a whole house, reaching 1.885 Gbps at 15 feet and still delivering 66.3 Mbps at a distant 90 feet. That kind of consistent performance means you won’t be left hunting for a signal in the farthest room.

In our testing, the Roamii BE Pro also excelled at mid-range distances, recording 815.2 Mbps at 50 feet — a result that puts it squarely among the fastest mesh systems we’ve seen.

Recent findings suggest that we found it outpaces the TP-Link Deco BE23 at close range (1.885 Gbps vs. 1.449 Gbps), but its real advantage is balancing those speeds with broader coverage, a feat some rivals like the Netgear Orbi 870 only match at longer distances. That makes the Roamii BE Pro a better pick for anyone who wants both fast speeds and reliable whole-home coverage, not just one or the other.

See our speed measurements tested at different distances.

During two weeks of everyday use, the Roamii BE Pro kept up without breaking a sweat. That includes streaming 4K video, downloading large files, gaming and emailing.

Plus, wired device fans get a trio of 2.5 Gbps LAN ports and a USB 3.0 port. It's just a shame that this isn't available in single or three-packs, meaning you'd have to buy another two-pack if you're looking to add more nodes. At least it isn't too pricey!

Setup is a breeze: after scanning the QR code, entering a network name and updating the firmware, I had both nodes running in just 15 minutes. If you want the quickest path to reliable, top-tier Wi-Fi 7 speeds without fuss, the Roamii BE Pro is the system to beat.

Sources indicate that the TP-Link Deco BE23 shows that high-speed, Wi-Fi 7 connectivity in a mesh system doesn't have to cost you a premium. For as low as $180, you can get a set of three powerful mesh networking devices that offer up far-reaching connectivity with some absolutely amazing speeds.

Industry observers note that each of the BE23 units comes in a neat, discreet design that can be placed anywhere while hiding in plain sight, and you can set up a connection for the whole house easily with TP-Link’s Deco app. Plus, any of the units can be used as a host router. Once you're set up, you can take control of your connectivity and devices via the app, like integrating and controlling Tapo, Kasa, Philips Hue and Matter home automation devices.

Speed is the star of the show, especially for this mesh system's affordable price. In our testing, we saw highs of 1.449 Gbps at 15 feet, and still 150.1 Mbps as far away as 90 feet. Those numbers beat many routers we've tested, even though it understandably falls behind the likes of a tri-band system (like the TP-Link Deco BE63 with 1.821 Gbps at 15 feet away).

In a recent development, with a maximum range of 115 feet for each unit, this mesh system will take you far (quite literally, connectivity-wise). Now that's an excellent balance between price and performance.

What you won't get here are more advanced features, like the 6 GHz band (just 2.4GHz and 5GHz here) or a super-wide 320 MHz data channel, and there's only a pair of 2.5 Gbps networking ports without a USB port, which makes wired connections limited.

For an affordable way to keep your whole home connected with fantastic internet speeds, the price is right with the TP-Link Deco BE23. It may not be the fastest or the most advanced, but for value, it's hard to go wrong with this mesh setup.

The Netgear Orbi 870 is a powerful mesh Wi-Fi system that really excels at medium and long ranges, even outperforming its larger, more expensive older sibling.

It has been revealed that despite its more premium price, I really like the more cylindrical design with a cleaner overall look of the Orbi 870 and the rest of the company’s Wi-Fi 7-powered mesh kits. While you’ll often see it in white at online retailers, you can actually get an all-black version too, but only on Netgear’s site.

In a recent development, the Orbi 870 is a very reliable and feature-packed mesh Wi-Fi system that’s ideal for futureproofing your home network thanks to its slew of multi-gig ports, including a 10 Gbps input. In his testing, Brian saw speeds of 1.82 Gbps at close range (15 feet).

In a recent development, however, it was the Orbi 870’s mid- and long-range performance that impressed him the most. For instance, at 50 and 75 feet, this mesh Wi-Fi system had download speeds of over 600 Mbps, beating both the entry-level Orbi 770 and even the Orbi 970 at the top of Netgear’s mesh lineup.

Industry observers note that even at a distance of 90 feet from Brian’s test laptop, it was at just over 100 Mbps, while the Orbi 970 and even TP-Link’s Deco BE85 were under 50 Mbps. At launch, a two-pack cost $1,000 (though you can often find it cheaper now), so the Orbi 870 is certainly an investment, just like the rest of the devices in Netgear’s Orbi line.

Sources indicate that however, if you have a large home you want to fill with a strong Wi-Fi signal and a top-tier multi-gig internet plan, it could definitely be worth it. Just keep in mind that you will need to set aside some extra cash if you want to secure your home network with it using Netgear’s Armor security package or want extended technical support, as only 90 days are included.

Sources indicate that the Acer Predator Connect T7 is a mesh Wi-Fi system with a heavy focus on gamers. However, unlike my previous mesh router pick for gaming, the Asus ROG Rapture GT6, it’s a Wi-Fi 7-powered device with a much more subtle look.

In a recent development, instead of RGB and lots of logos, the Predator Connect T7 features a taller, rectangular design in white or black, and at first glance, it looks quite similar to an Xbox Series X. There’s a splash of RGB lighting on the top, but this mesh kit has a sleeker and more restrained look that I think definitely works in its favor.

Industry observers note that just like with the best gaming routers, the Predator Connect T7 has a low-latency design that uses Intel’s Killer Prioritization engine for peak gaming performance. It also comes with free built-in security software and makes full use of all of Wi-Fi 7’s best features.

According to recent reports, during testing, Brian saw download speeds of 1.9 Gbps at close range (15 feet) with good mid-range performance. While the Predator Connect T7 has a multi-gig input port, its wired Ethernet ports are limited to gigabit speeds, so plugging in one of the best gaming laptops won’t give you a significant speed boost over connecting via Wi-Fi.

The Acer Predator Connect T7 is one of the few mesh Wi-Fi systems specifically designed for gamers and if you want a mesh router that looks as slick as your gaming PC, it’s a big step up from the Asus ROG Rapture GT7 (which superseded the GT6 we used to recommend).

However, it is on the expensive side at $330 per device, and unlike other mesh kits, you won’t see any discounts at all when buying a multi-pack. Still, if you want gaming-level network performance with the added benefits of mesh and want something less flashy, the Predator Connect T7 is an excellent mesh Wi-Fi system and the only one for gamers with Wi-Fi 7 support so far.

It has been revealed that the Eero Pro 7 is a smaller and sleeker mesh Wi-Fi system that’s incredibly simple to set up and use. Unlike Eero’s past mesh kits, which had a puck-shaped design, this one has a rounded rectangular shape and, at 7.1 x 5.8 x 2.6 inches, you won’t have any trouble finding a place for it and its satellites around your home.

Industry observers note that after testing the larger, more powerful Eero Max 7 myself, I really like the Pro 7’s more compact design and the fact that it's significantly cheaper, too. The biggest selling point of the Pro 7 and Eero’s other mesh Wi-Fi systems is that even a home networking novice will have no trouble at all getting them up and running.

Setup and configuration are handled entirely through the very user-friendly Eero app. Besides how it looks, I really like the way that updates are downloaded and installed automatically, so your mesh Wi-Fi system is always running the latest software.

In his testing, Brian saw download speeds of 1.9 Gbps at close distances (15 feet), but the Pro 7 was equally impressive at mid-range distances with speeds just under a gigabit.

The Eero Pro 7 does cost a bit more than the competition, but nowhere close to what you’d pay for an Orbi mesh kit. As an Amazon company, Eero works great with your Alexa-powered and other smart home devices, and you can even use an Echo Dot as a mesh extender to add some extra range to your home network.

Recent findings suggest that if you want a fast and capable Wi-Fi 7-powered mesh system that’s simple to set up and just works, the Eero Pro 7 is very easy to recommend, especially since it's a lot cheaper than the Max 7. The one downside is that you’re limited to just two Ethernet ports, but they are the faster 5 Gbps variety, which is great if you have a multi-gig internet blueprint.

According to recent reports, the TP-Link Deco BE85 is a top-of-the-line mesh Wi-Fi system that was actually the first mesh router with Wi-Fi 7 support. It builds on the cylindrical design of the Deco XE75 with a more refined and polished look, but it packs in a ton of multi-gig and even a USB port.

Sources indicate that as someone who upgraded to fiber internet, I love how it has its own SFP+ port, which lets you plug your fiber line directly in at the back instead of into a separate ONT box first. Even if you’re still using one of the best cable modems, though, the Deco BE85 is a powerful mesh Wi-Fi system that won’t disappoint when it comes to performance.

According to recent reports, one thing that’s really convenient about this mesh kit and TP-Link’s other Deco devices is that they’re all identical out of the box and you can use any of them as your main router. The firm’s Deco app also makes setup and configuration very easy, and in my experience, it’s on par with Eero’s app in terms of usability.

15 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 1.736.

50 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 790.4.

75 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 179.2.

90 feet (Toms Guide): TP-Link Deco BE85 scores 42.6.

In a recent development, during testing, Brian saw download speeds of 1.73 Gbps at a close distance (15 feet) and good mid-range speeds, too. While this might seem a bit low for a premium mesh Wi-Fi system, Brian was one of the first people to get and review the Deco BE85. It's possible this has improved with firmware updates since its launch.

The Deco BE85 has come down in price since it introduced, but it’s still expensive, even though this model does go on sale quite frequently. However, if you have a fast, multi-gig fiber internet blueprint and want top-notch Wi-Fi 7 performance, this mesh router is the only one I’ve seen yet with an SFP+ port on the back.

It’s worth noting that, just like with Eero, all TP-Link Deco devices are compatible with one another, so you could always mix and match or upgrade to a more powerful model later on if you need to.

Sources indicate that the mesh Wi-Fi systems we've used all come with amazing speeds, and we've done the testing to show how fast a router is at short and long ranges. But you'll find some will perform better at various distances, even if one delivers the fastest speeds around.

As an example, the Acer Predator Connect T7 offers the fastest speeds at 15 feet, but it loses out to the likes of the TP-Link Deco BE23 and others at 90 feet. It comes down to what you prioritize: speed or range (or a balance of both!).

So, to compare each mesh Wi-Fi system across the range of distances we've tested, check out the versus table below to help you make the right choice for your home.

Select a mesh Wi-Fi system to compare internet speed at different distances (measured in Gbps and Mbps).

Sources indicate that we test every mesh Wi-Fi system to measure performance and range, using Keysight IxChariot. Testing is done in a multi-story home with brick walls. When we test standard routers, we look at performance at a distance to provide real-world information about coverage and speeds. In addition to lab testing, we evaluate the ease of setup and features of each device, too.

According to recent reports, we measure performance at a 15-foot distance without obstructions, so that we can gauge the maximum amount of data that a router can move. Higher throughput will serve you better in data-heavy uses, like streaming video, gaming, or connecting multiple people at once.

It has been revealed that range measures the furthest usable distance for a particular router. Longer ranges are better for larger homes, where rooms are spread out at a distance. We measure how much data a router can move at 15, 50, 75 and 90 feet, as well as the maximum coverage area of a mesh Wi-Fi system.

Industry observers note that we also test how well each mesh Wi-Fi system transmits and receives signals through drywall, brick, concrete and even metal walls, and how each handles coverage in a two- or three-story home. They also go through additional testing to see how well each system does when sending a signal through the main router and through the included satellites.

Of course (and most importantly), we also consider what you really get for your money, considering which features are worthwhile and how any given product compares with other devices from competing manufacturers.

It has been revealed that A lot of factors come into choosing the mesh Wi-Fi system that will suit your space, from the coverage you need to the speeds you demand — all for the right price. We've got just the tips to make your choice easier.

Wi-Fi 8 is right now still in the early stages of being supported on all devices, so you won't be able to take advantage of the latest connectivity standard right now. Currently, no consumer devices support Wi-Fi 8 coverage, and we're not expecting to see support until sometime in 2027 or 2028.

Industry observers note that we've reviewed the first Wi-Fi 8 router, the Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro, and are impressed by its incredible Wi-Fi speeds and range. However, we couldn't see its full potential since we're still waiting for Wi-Fi 8 hardware. We'll have to see how well mesh Wi-Fi systems with Wi-Fi 8 perform, too.

In a recent development, while Wi-Fi 8 isn't worth getting right now, it may be worth it to many looking to future-proof their homes once more devices adopt Wi-Fi 8. Besides, it's backwards compatible with Wi-Fi 7, Wi-Fi 6 and so on. We'll keep you updated in the meantime.

Yes, a mesh Wi-Fi system can go through walls. Because Wi-Fi uses radio waves, these waves can pass through solid materials like walls to connect to a device.

However, when Wi-Fi meets a wall, some of it goes through, some bounces off and some is absorbed. Because of this, the signal can be weaker, especially when more walls are in the way.

In a recent development, A mesh Wi-Fi system has an advantage in getting past this. Instead of using one router to get a signal, a mesh system uses multiple nodes placed throughout a home to bypass hard objects or walls in order to get an unobstructed signal. This means there are fewer barriers to getting a clear Wi-Fi signal.

The main downside of using a mesh Wi-Fi system is that it can be very expensive, especially compared to traditional Wi-Fi routers. These are only needed for those living in large homes or for anyone who needs Wi-Fi coverage over a long distance. For those in smaller spaces, this is overkill.

Since mesh systems come in a multi-pack of nodes, this bumps up the price, as these extra devices deliver a better range of coverage throughout a space compared to other routers.

Sources indicate that nodes also must be placed close enough to catch a strong signal, which can be tricky in a home with many rooms separated by concrete or brick walls. Plus, with this signal hopping between multiple nodes, there may be an increase in latency, which isn't ideal for competitive gameplay.

Otherwise, the best mesh Wi-Fi systems try to overcome these downsides, and these are still the best option to upgrade your home network wirelessly.

In a recent development, mesh Wi-Fi systems come with nodes and are usually available in two-packs or three-packs, but deciding which one to get depends on the size of your home. If you live in a small or medium house, then a two-pack will usually do the trick. For large homes with more than three bedrooms or multiple stories, a three-pack is the better choice, as this will ensure that your Wi-Fi signal reaches every corner and even upstairs.

Recent findings suggest that the great thing about mesh Wi-Fi systems, though, is that you can always start small and work up to something bigger. For instance, if you buy a two-pack and find that you’re still dealing with Wi-Fi dead zones in certain parts of your home, you can always add another node later to improve your coverage.

Plug-in Wi-Fi extenders aren’t nearly as advanced or as powerful as the nodes in a mesh Wi-Fi system. The other big problem with Wi-Fi extenders is that most of them create a separate network you have to manually switch to each time you want to use them. For instance, let’s say you put a Wi-Fi extender in your bedroom. Whenever you want to get online in that particular room, you’ll have to switch from your main Wi-Fi network to the extender, which gets annoying really fast.

Recent findings suggest that on the other hand, with a mesh Wi-Fi system, the nodes are all part of your main network and no switching is required. As you move from one side of your house to the other, your mesh system automatically hands off your connection to whatever satellite you’re closest to, which ensures you have a strong signal and a good connection wherever you are in your home.

As someone who's been working from home for the past eight years, Anthony Spadafora has tried everything from Wi-Fi extenders to powerline adapters to get the most out of his home network, before finally upgrading to a mesh Wi-Fi system. Along the way, he's tested out loads of different routers and network configurations. Based on what he's learned, Anthony tries to highlight the critical role Wi-Fi routers play in our day-to-day lives and how a mesh network can help solve the most common connectivity challenges like Wi-Fi dead spots.

Industry observers note that with experience in testing, using and evaluating wireless data from before Wi-Fi was even a word, Brian Nadel has tried out and reviewed every major router available in his home networking lab. A LAN nerd, his philosophy is to use the router the way you would, testing networking gear for ease of setup, performance, security and above all for value. The result is peace of mind when it comes to choosing the right router.

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were announced in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

The idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

It has been revealed that fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the new version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

Before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

In iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

Industry observers note that that’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

According to recent reports, the only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Have you been using iOS 27’s Smart Reply feature in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

In a recent development, A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that shows up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

It has been revealed that “Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

In the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

It’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

Industry observers note that the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

It has been revealed that lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

Sources indicate that if you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

If you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the firm is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

Sources indicate that the standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):.

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Industry observers note that amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

In a recent development, A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

It has been revealed that amazon Health: Prime consumers get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance plans, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers upcoming free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

In a recent development, ❌ Tiny viewfinder: The Ultra F9 35mm has a very small viewfinder located right above the film door on the back. Those who wear glasses may struggle to look through it.

Overall, the Kodak Ultra F9 35mm is a fantastic choice for those starting out in film photography. It’s reusable so after the initial spend, you’ll just need to spend money on batteries and film — neither of which cost a lot. It’s easy to use, compact and portable, and it produces charming retro photos, all of which make it the best cheap camera for film lovers.

It has been revealed that "This is my favorite cheap film camera because it takes great photos and can be used by practically anyone. It's the perfect way to dabble in film without spending much money.".

See Kodak F9 35mm sample images.

One-line review: The Camp Snap CS-Pro is a pocket-friendly compact digital camera that we took quite literally everywhere in testing. It takes 16MP pictures that look pretty decent, but the big selling point for this is the lack of screen, keeping you firmly in the moment at all times.

The Camp Snap CS-Pro is the ideal for anyone who wants to capture their adventures. Because of the lack of an LCD screen to preview photos, you won’t be caught up in how your pictures look, and you can simply enjoy the moment. Any fans of the original Camp Snap Screen-Free Camera will love this model too, as the CS-Pro features quality upgrades (including double the sensor resolution) and four new color filter settings.

It can go anywhere with complete ease thanks to its compact size and light weight. Trust me, we tried. In testing, we took it to music concerts, on hiking trails, and out with friends. It held up in every situation and looked good while doing so. It may feel a little plasticky but this keeps the weight down. It takes great photos and demonstrated strong performance in a variety of lighting scenarios during testing, so wherever your travels take you, the camera will be ready.

Sources indicate that ✅ Color filters: The color filter dial on this camera offers four settings to add a little whimsy to the camera. This means you can even experiment a little with such a simple camera.

✅ Lightweight: At 5.12 ounces, this is one of the lightest digital cameras you can buy, making it ideal for throwing in your bag without being bulky.

✅ Easy to use: It’s a point-and-shoot camera, so there’s not much to it. But the lack of a screen means that you don’t even need to worry about how your shots look in the moment.

✅ Long battery life: It has a rated battery life of 500 shots, but we were able to get even better performance in testing.

❌ Shutter lag: This is vastly improved from the previous model, but there is still a shutter response delay when taking pictures in quick succession, which can prove annoying if you’re trying to get the perfect shot.

❌ Offset viewfinder: The viewfinder of the camera is set slightly to the left of the lens, so if you use this to frame your shots, you need to compensate a little, as your framing will be off.

According to recent reports, the Camp Snap CS-Pro is the perfect travel addition for making memories without the distraction of a screen. Its small size and low weight make it a great option for anyone who doesn’t want a camera that takes up a lot of space. It holds up well in most lighting conditions and offers a reliable solution for fun photography with four color settings to choose from. It comes with me everywhere.

Industry observers note that "The Camp Snap CS-Pro is the perfect choice for anyone who wants to make memories on a budget. The newly introduced model has even had a stylish looks upgrade, double the resolution, and new color filters that make photography so much fun!".

One-line review: A cheap and extremely cheerful point-and-shoot that feels like something from 30 years ago and takes lovely pictures.

Sources indicate that someone who wants to take snaps on holiday and doesn't mind if they can't see them until they plug their SD card into their laptop. This is about as "point and shoot" as it gets — if you want a screen to check things, you'll want something a bit different to this little retro hero.

The Camp Snap 2 is a super portable little camera, and it boils down the act of photography to its most basic parts. It's extremely easy to use — you pop your eye up to the viewfinder, point the camera at your subject, and press the shutter button. Its retro charm is hard to ignore, and the 500 snap battery life is good too. Oh, and it takes really nice images with a nostalgic twinge.

✅ Compact, lightweight design: Measuring only 1.3 x 2.5 x 4.5 inches, the Camp Snap 2 will fit into any pocket you like — and weighing only 3.8 ounces, you won't even know it's there.

✅ Super simple to use: Put your eye to the viewfinder and press the shutter button. This is about as easy to use as it gets.

✅ Good image quality: There's a wonderful retro charm to the images that the Camp Snap 2 takes — and they're bright and colorful to boot.

❌ Plasticky build: This is a cheap retro camera — don't expect sumptuous materials or premium build quality.

❌ Laggy shutter: Pressing the shutter button doesn't immediately activate the shutter. There's a slightly irritating delay.

Recent findings suggest that this is a cheap, cheap camera that's packed full of fun features. The lack of a screen might seem like a problem, but it really reconnects you with the act of taking a photo — and the images themselves are great too. Why is it the best point-and-shoot camera? Because it does two things, and it does them both very well. It points, and it shoots.

"I love the Camp Snap 2 and its retro styling — the fun nostalgic filters are loads of fun too.".

One-line review: Despite its tiny stature and budget price, the DJI Neo is absolutely stuffed to the brim with features and doesn't require FAA registration.

The DJI Neo is for drone novices or enthusiasts on a budget who are looking to enter the world of drone photography. For the features it offers, this drone is excellent value for money.

The Neo is great for those starting out in drone photography because everything is done automatically — from exposure to ISO. It’s extremely easy to fly either with your smartphone or the RC-N3 controller, and its small size makes it the perfect travel companion. The Neo is capable of shooting 4K video at 30fps and capturing 12MP stills. It has been succeeded by the DJI Neo 2, but that drone is quite a bit pricier, so we still favor the original Neo for this guide.

✅ Easy to fly: You can control the Neo either via the DJI Fly app on a smartphone or the RC-N3 controller, and both ways are straightforward. The RC-N3 comes with two detachable joysticks which are highly responsive and comfortable to use for long hours.

✅ User-friendly app: DJI's app is free to download and easy to use, while also providing lots of functionality and control.

In a recent development, ✅ Compact and lightweight: The Neo weighs just 4.76 ounces which means you don’t need to obtain a license to fly it (but it’s still worth checking local laws before flying). This also means it’s very easy to travel with.

✅ Smooth 4K footage: The Neo shoots 4K video at 30fps or 1080P at 60fps, which is great for the price. Footage is smooth with plenty of detail, as is panning across a scene. Its f/2.8 aperture also delivers good results in moderately lit conditions.

✅ Very affordable: At under $200, this is one of the cheapest and best drones you can buy.

❌ Short flight time: On a single charge, the Neo has a flight time of just 18 minutes which is about half the time you get with DJI’s other drones. It’s worth investing in the Fly More combo which gives you two spare batteries to bump the total flying time up to 54 minutes.

It has been revealed that ❌ No obstacle avoidance: Unlike pricier DJI drones, the Neo doesn’t feature smart obstacle avoidance. This means that the drone can’t automatically dodge walls or trees, so you’ll have to be mindful of its position in the air at all times.

Recent findings suggest that the Neo is a beginner-friendly drone that doesn’t cost a fortune, making it the ideal choice for aerial enthusiasts. The ability to capture gorgeous 4K footage and detailed stills, combined with its ease of use and lightweight body, makes the Neo the best cheap drone camera.

"The DJI Neo may not be the latest DJI beginner drone, but it still boasts fantastic specs and features for beginner pilots, all at a price that can't be beat.".

It has been revealed that panasonic Lumix G97 ★★★★Considered for: Best cheap mirrorless cameraThe Lumix G97 is a great little camera, that produces solid images, offers decent handling and even boasts a form of IBIS (but only when paired with an OIS lens). Its AF is out of date for a modern camera, though, so we prefer the Canon EOS R100 for our best cheap mirrorless award.

Sources indicate that potensic Atom 2 ★★★★½Considered for: Best cheap droneThe Potensic Atom 2 is the closest competitor to the DJI Neo in the cheap, entry-level drones category. We loved its 4K video, 48MP stills, AI subject tracking and intuitive controller. At the end of the day though, the DJI Neo, which is also an epic drone, won for one simple reason: it's cheaper.

Pentax WG-1000 ★★★★Considered for: Best cheap rugged cameraWe liked the Pentax WG-1000 during testing. It shot decent stills and was indeed rugged. However, it's more expensive than the Kodak PIXPRO WPZ2 but doesn't offer much more.

Fujifilm Instax mini 12 ★★★★Considered for: Best cheap instant cameraAh, the legendary Instax mini 12. Make no mistake, we love this camera, and it holds the best for beginners award on our roundup of the best instant cameras. However, the Polaroid Go Gen 2 (holds the top spot on our instant cams roundup) offers a lot more for very little extra cash.

When buying a cheap camera, you’re naturally going to have to sacrifice a few things. The latest and greatest cameras simply don’t come cheap. Usually, you’ll either have to accept an older model, or sacrifice features.

Recent findings suggest that however, you absolutely don’t have to sacrifice quality. You can pick up some great cameras for well under $100, and they aren’t just cheap crap. And that’s where we come in! This guide is designed to help you filter out the cameras that are cheap, yet still great quality and built to last.

The specific features you need to look for will depend on what you’re using the camera for. If you want to take really nice photos and grow as a photographer, then you’ll want a camera with a larger sensor, decent megapixel count and good autofocus — that means you’ll need to splash out on a DSLR or mirrorless camera.

Shooting video? You’ll want 4K footage, decent stabilization and the ability to connect external microphones. A vlogging camera is ideal, or an action camera if you’ll be shooting outdoors or in extreme environments. If you’re after sky-high footage, then you’ll want a drone (and yes, you can absolutely pick up great drones without breaking the bank).

Sources indicate that want to print your photos? You have a few options. The high-resolution sensors in mirrorless cameras will yield the best results when printing digital images. If you want the film look, you can go for an instant camera, which will be best for immediate printing and documenting social events, or a film camera, which will produce higher quality prints but requires film to be developed.

If you need a camera for travel, then it’s all about portability. You’ll want something that takes decent photos, but is small enough to fit in a pocket or backpack, and which won’t become a chore when worn around your neck.

According to recent reports, every single camera on this list has been through the Tom’s Guide reviews process, which means they’ve all been thoroughly tested by Tom’s Guide experts. The testing process naturally differs for the different categories of cameras — we test an action camera differently to how we test an instant camera, for example.

In a recent development, however, there are many things all cameras have in common. We always test how sharp the camera optics are, looking for optical distortions and image artefacts. We always evaluate how well images turn out, how detailed they are and the color accuracy of the camera. We take lots of test shots or videos with each camera, enabling us to test autofocus, exposure metering and all the extra features such as AF modes.

Industry observers note that naturally, we always evaluate the price of a product, test its build quality, and analyze both how easy the camera is to use and how sensibly it’s laid out. If there’s a smartphone app, we use it and evaluate how many extra features it adds, but also how user-friendly it is. We always evaluate the battery life of cameras, too.

We don’t just list the specs or features of these cameras either, and always analyze whether each of a camera’s features is good or bad, and why — that involves weighing it up against the product’s cost and competition. Throughout each review, we constantly compare each product to its rivals to help you make the most informed purchase. We’ve included links to the individual reviews for each camera within every entry, so you can get the full lowdown on each product if you want to know more.

Why spend money on even a cheap camera when you have your smartphone, right? Won't your phone take pictures just as well?

That depends on the phone and indeed the camera, but generally speaking a decent dedicated camera will be able to take better photos than your smartphone. Phones have small image sensors, as there isn't much space inside a phone case for a large sensor. The iPhone 16 uses a 1/1.29-inch sensor, which is a lot smaller than the APS-C sensor used in the Canon EOS R100. A larger sensor delivers cleaner images in low light. That remarked, many phones these days feature larger sensors than some cameras, especially compact cameras.

In a recent development, another factor is optics. Smartphones have to use small lenses — again, as space is a major consideration. Smaller lenses just can't match the sharpness and quality of larger lenses on dedicated cameras, especially those on interchangeable lens cameras (like mirrorless or DSLR bodies).

And while some smartphones offer manual controls, often these aren't truly manual. You can adjust "aperture" on an iPhone, for instance, but the phone simply applies a software-generated blur to approximate the look of a shallow depth of field at wide apertures. While this looks OK at a glance, study the image closely and you'll see mistakes and things blurred that shouldn't be. This reliance on software is repeated in other areas by your smartphone camera, and generally results in poorer image quality.

It has been revealed that and finally, there's use case. If you want to shoot film photos, or print your photos instantly, you can't do either with a smartphone alone. Using a dedicated camera is often more fun, too! There's something special about the experience of using a camera that smartphones can't quite replicate.

That really depends on the category of camera you need, and the definition of “cheap” changes based on stated category. If you want the best image quality or a vlogging camera, you’ll need a mirrorless camera like the EOS R100, and cheap means around the $250-$400 mark. Action cameras, expect to spend around $175 - $200 for a cheap model.

Great instant cameras and compact cameras can easily be found for around the $100 mark, while affordable film cameras can be yours for very little more. If you want a cheap drone, you can expect to spend in the vicinity of $200.

No. Or at least, not until they're sure they want to get into photography. Cheap cameras are a great way to see if you like photography (or shooting video), and whether you really want to put in the time and dedication to learn and gain experience.

Recent findings suggest that that's not to say you should buy the cheapest camera you can find, though, as there are many terrible cameras out there which are a total waste of money. You should buy a decent camera which will allow you to learn without breaking the bank. And that's where this guide comes in! It will help you choose a cheap camera that's also good quality.

AirPods 5 vs AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy this holiday season?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts.
  • Industry observers note that airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions.
  • The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

Industry observers note that airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

According to recent reports, the key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that if you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

According to recent reports, airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

Sources indicate that if you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

In a recent development, this year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

In a recent development, airPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

Sources indicate that if you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

Industry News: These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1475 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 newly introduced features—including one feature the manufacturer trialed in the previous beta.

Recent findings suggest that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger challenges. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this fresh feature here.

iOS 27.3 also comes with a newly introduced setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Currently, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the significant screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a latest set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally confirmed with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

The company generated some controversy when it first confirmed these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these fresh Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company states Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These newly introduced actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

According to recent reports, apple started testing its upcoming Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Recent findings suggest that continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a newly introduced Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training initiative. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

In a recent development, vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another upcoming Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

According to recent reports, apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

Industry observers note that "Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Recent findings suggest that apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

Recent findings suggest that if you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

According to recent reports, if you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

Breaking: These are the best noise canceling earbuds we've tested that are actually worth your money right now
