Latest Update: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2982 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Sources indicate that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Sources indicate that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Recent findings suggest that the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

It has been revealed that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Industry observers note that “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

It has been revealed that more than 10 years in the making, MMX released on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a fresh rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” notes Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to strategy, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” notes Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

It has been revealed that from that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

Industry observers note that the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

According to recent reports, during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

According to recent reports, before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu states, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

It has been revealed that idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

In a recent development, “It will bounce probably several times,” notes Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

According to recent reports, A simulation demonstrates how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

Industry observers note that the WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

Sources indicate that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday notes.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday claims Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

In a recent development, idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

According to recent reports, what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

In a recent development, once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

Industry observers note that the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

Sources indicate that the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel notes. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Recent findings suggest that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

According to recent reports, the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this glitch and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu notes.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Recent findings suggest that that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Industry observers note that once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel states. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

Sources indicate that “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

  • Apple made a bunch of changes to iOS to optimize it for the iPhone Duo’s form factor, including revamping the Lock Screen.
  • Recent findings suggest that 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upgrade: It turns out that this feature is actually referenced in the User Guide for iPhone Duo.

Apple made a bunch of changes to iOS to optimize it for the iPhone Duo’s form factor, including revamping the Lock Screen. According to a latest leak today, the organization has tested another change, referred to as a “complication column.” Here’s what it looks like.

Recent findings suggest that 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

On the iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen right now, you can add widgets along the bottom of the interface. On the bottom right, you have two controls that default to the flashlight and camera. You can customize these and link them to other controls from Apple and third-party apps.

Cellular and Wi-Fi information is located along the top right-hand side of the iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen.

Sources indicate that according to the spelunking account pdfu on X, Apple has tested a “complication column” that would appear along the right edge of the Lock Screen. The column has room for two widgets, filling the space between the flashlight/camera controls and the Wi-Fi and cellular status icons. These widgets are the same size as the widgets that appear along the bottom.

The “complication column” for iPhone Duo was first spotted in iOS 27.1 code, the account indicates. No code changes have been made since, so it’s unclear whether the feature is still in active development or Apple has scrapped it.

Recent findings suggest that apple has tested a “complication column” for iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen. It fits two circular widgets along the right edge.Flag: SpringBoard/Ionic (disabled). First seen in iOS 27.1, with no code changes since. pic.twitter.com/orjOuvM1Xs.

I think this looks great. It’s fun seeing Apple try different things as it learns how to best design for the iPhone Duo’s form factor, which is so different from a traditional iPhone. I’d be especially intrigued to try this on the inner display’s Lock Screen, where there’s right now a lot of wasted space.

I hope this “complication column” idea is still in development and makes it into a future iOS 27 update. What about you? Let us know down in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that sunrise on the Reaping already is heading to an estimated $16M, which is both the best Tuesday Lionsgate has ever seen for a movie and also a franchise record for the day, besting Catching Fire’s $15.96M in 2013.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will have all the fire to keep the Thanksgiving box office stretch cooking with at least $70M at the domestic B.O. between Wednesday and Sunday, per industry estimates. Five-day forecasts are hard, duh, and only once we’re into Black Friday — the richest day of the frame — does it become apparent how much overdrive is in the box office.

Industry observers note that sunrise on the Reaping already is heading to an estimated $16M, which is both the best Tuesday Lionsgate has ever seen for a movie and also a franchise record for the day, besting Catching Fire’s $15.96M in 2013. The day also is bound to be higher than Wicked: For Good‘s first Tuesday a year ago, which was $15.7M. That will take the Francis Lawrence-directed pic’s running cume through five days to $148.2M, $18.1M away from overtaking the $166.3M lifetime North American total on the previous Hunger Games film, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, three years ago.

In a recent development, remember, Sunrise on the Reaping will cede some of its Imax screens, specifically AMC’s, to Netflix’s limited run of the Brad Pitt-starring The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. The Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel will be booked at 250 locations for a two-week run and arrive on Netflix 28 days after its Wednesday bow. The David Fincher -directed featured penned by Quentin Tarantino is 82% certified fresh on Rotten Tomatoes with critics (Once Upon a Time in Hollywood was 86% certified fresh) and is looking at single digits over 5 days. Last year, Netflix’s Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery only made $4M over the Wednesday-Sunday stretch at 600 locations. Watch on Deadline.

Among the new stuff, Walt Disney Animation’s original animated title Hexed should be stronger than Universal/Paramount’s Focker-in-Law when it comes to global openings (5-day domestic + the regular foreign weekend of Wednesday to Sunday), $75M-$80M WW to $70M.

Domestically right now via Universal, the bet is that the added high note of Ariana Grande to the 26-year-old Ben Stiller-Robert De Niro Meet the Parents comedy franchise will have the upper hand with a $45M Wednesday to Sunday (there aren’t any Tuesday night previews, through showtimes start at midnight) at 3,350 theaters, despite awful reviews at 28% Rotten. Reviews always have been bad for the Fockers films, except for the 2000 original, which stands at 85% certified fresh. Uni will have some PLFs. Women over 25 are best in first choice, followed by women under 25 and men over 25.

In the $90M net production, which was evenly co-bankrolled by Uni and Paramount, Greg Focker’s son, Henry (Skyler Gisondo), brings his girlfriend (Grande), a trained FBI hostage negotiator, home to meet the family. Greg (Stiller) soon gets worried when Henry tells everyone that he plans to propose to her. Paramount is a co-financier here, having inherited the property from the days when its had an interest in DreamWorks, the previous co-studio on the franchise.

Industry observers note that paramount overseas will release Focker-in-Law in 62 territories except for Japan. Comps abroad for comedies, particularly, non-grossout films, are hard. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers.
  • Recent findings suggest that because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives.
  • In a recent development, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Recent findings suggest that because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

In a recent development, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the manufacturer introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

According to recent reports, if you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's at the moment pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, presently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

Recent findings suggest that if you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (at the moment $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

For about $30 more than the X4 Classic, you can upgrade to the Xteink X4 Pro, which happens to be Lifehacker's e-reader Gift of the Year pick. It offers all the perks of the other Xteink devices, with two critical quality-of-life upgrades: A touchscreen for easier navigation, and a temperature-adjustable front light so you can read it in a dark room. (Less obviously, it also has a slightly faster processor that makes the whole thing feel a little snappier.) Right now, the X4 Pro is at its lowest price ever when ordered directly from Xteink: $84, or around 15% off the usual $99 price.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

iOS 27 includes a really clever upcoming feature that aims to solve the awkward middle ground between cellular and Wi-Fi connectivity. Here’s how it works and how you can turn it on.

Industry observers note that in a support document, Apple explains that Connectivity Assist uses cellular data to improve your connection when Wi-Fi is slow or unusable. Apple uses examples like your backyard or driveway, as well as “coffee shops, airports, sports venues, and everywhere in between.”.

Essentially, the feature detects when your Wi-Fi connection is weak or unusable and intelligently uses cellular data to keep you connected.

One practical example I’ve noticed is when I walk out of my house and get in my car. Oftentimes, my iPhone will cling to my house’s weak Wi-Fi connection, making it hard to start playing Apple Music and queue up directions in Apple Maps.

Industry observers note that connectivity Assist solves that problem. My phone can now intelligently use cellular data to help that transition away from Wi-Fi. It’s one of many really nice quality-of-life improvements in iOS 27.

Five recent tech outages were not due to AI; the next round will be

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.
  • That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….
  • Earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….

Earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated concerns coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication glitch affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith indicates it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

“We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us,” the studio head told Entertainment Weekly. “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.”.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then highlights how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far.
  • Industry observers note that I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are crucial.
  • Industry observers note that if you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far. The world feels even more detailed and immersive than previous GTA games, which means there's a lot to learn beyond the basic tutorials and prompts the game shares at the beginning. These are the 10 GTA 6 hacks I used to improve the game's quality of life. If you do the same, you'll spend more time immersed in the world, and less time fighting the game's default settings.

Industry observers note that I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are crucial. If you ignore all the optional quests or small asks by other characters, you won't be able to return to those later. These are small things like fixing up the house for Lucia, meditating with her, and buying her a necklace when she asks you to. All of these have an impact on your progress. Take your time in this chapter, and remember to save before starting the mission called "Recalibration." That mission leads to Tourist Trap, which is the point of no return for Chapter 1.

Industry observers note that if you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different. It's hard to keep an eye on minimap directions while you're also getting used to vehicles in the game, and I used voice navigation to ensure that I don't keep getting lost, particularly for time-sensitive missions. You can enable this by going to GTA VI settings > Audio > GPS Voice > Voice. If you're playing the game on PS5, your DualSense controller's speaker plays GPS voice prompts. This is great as those alerts can be hard to hear over all other in-game sounds from your TV's speaker.

It has been revealed that using GTA 6's default controls, making Jason and Lucia run is quite annoying. The game makes you hold L3 to run, which hurts my thumbs. If you alter movement speed in settings, you can make the characters run just by using the left stick. You can walk by easing off the left stick, or switch to a fast walk, jog, or run when you push the stick all the way. Tweak this by going to GTA VI settings > Gameplay > Movement Speed > Jog. This lets you move faster without draining your stamina. You can also change from Jog to Run if you want the fastest possible movement speed with the left stick. Having said that, my pro tip is to go to Control Scheme in settings, and switch to Classic. This lets you run by holding the X button, as opposed to L3 with default controls.

It has been revealed that haptic strength is one area where GTA 6 takes the immersion a bit too far, as it's dialed up to the maximum level by default. This makes the controller's vibration strength a bit too intense for my liking, and also has a negative impact on battery life. You can fix that by reducing haptic strength a little. It's under GTA VI settings > Controller > Vibration & Haptics Strength.

It has been revealed that many modern controllers develop "stick drift," an issue where small movements of the analog sticks register as large inputs. This causes a significant problem in games that require precise inputs, such as GTA 6. To counter this potential problem, the game allows you to adjust the deadzone for each analog stick in your controller. That said, this setting can be used to your advantage, even if you don't have stick drift issues in your controller. I recommend dialing up the deadzone to 7 to improve the driving experience. I find most cars in GTA 6 to be a bit floaty to drive, and adjusting the deadzone fixes this issue to a large extent.

Sources indicate that committing a heist attracts heat in GTA 6, and there are many different ways to escape the attention of in-game cops. The usual tricks include stocking up on outfits to change into, parking your vehicle a block or two away, and being so stealthy that you leave no witnesses to your crimes. However, an underrated trick involves using the pickup truck you get at the start of the game. Get a bike in the game, and stash it in your pickup truck. Then, use the truck to drive to the crime scene, and hide the truck a short distance away. Unload the bike, and use it to get to the crime scene. Once the heist is complete, ditch the bike, and run to your truck. Witnesses won't have seen you using the truck, which allows you to escape the area quickly.

In a recent development, if you are using a car as a getaway vehicle, you can use two tricks to make a smooth escape. First, double-tap the Triangle button to exit your vehicle without switching off its engine. When you return to the vehicle in a hurry, you can escape a lot faster. If you have quick fingers, you can double-tap Triangle first, and just as your character is about to exit the vehicle, press L3 (or X, if you use classic controls). This leaves the car's door open, and saves you a little more time when you're fleeing.

Sources indicate that I suffer from chronic migraines, and I am sensitive to bright lights. Fortunately, GTA 6 has a bunch of accessibility settings that help me play the game for longer. Even if you don't face the same issues, these settings will help reduce eye strain in longer play sessions. Go to GTA VI settings > Display > Flashbang, and switch to Dark. This stops flashbangs from showing a bright white light when they go off. On the same settings page, you can tweak Player Status Effects Intensity to reduce screen effects when your character is low on health or stamina. You can also enable Brightness Reduction to reduce the intensity of bright lights in the game, and try Focus Trail Colorblind Mode if you find it hard to distinguish between different colors.

I haven't been able to play first-person shooters for decades because the camera movement makes me nauseous and gives me a headache. Of late, I've noticed that it's getting harder to play third-person games too. My first two hours in GTA 6 had me quite worried because I was feeling quite sick, and I had to turn off my PS5. Luckily for me, I found a few tweaks to mitigate this problem. You can do that in GTA VI settings > UI > Persistent Center Dot. This permanently shows a white dot in the center of the screen, and it reduced my motion sickness enough to help me play the game. You can also go to GTA VI settings > Camera, reduce Camera Bob, and turn off Camera Shake, and Weapon Sway. I also recommend going to the Controller tab in settings, and tweaking all the options under Aim & Look Sensitivity until you find a comfortable level.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 includes realistic ringing sounds that linger after explosions in the game. This may be fine for some people, but it can negatively affect some players' gaming sessions. Those who suffer from tinnitus or chronic migraines may not enjoy those ringing sounds, and, luckily, the game allows you to disable them. Open GTA 6's in-game settings, and enable the feature from Audio > Tinnitus Reduction.

#97005. GTA 6 is a generational masterpiece — and one of the few games I’ve given a perfect score in 16 years

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2754 w)
📖 Baca

GTA 6 is a generational masterpiece — and one of the few games I’ve given a perfect score in 16 years

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is easily the most impressive entry in the (in)famous series and a technical showcase that raises the bar for open-world games.
  • Sources indicate that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you.
  • Platforms: PS5 (reviewed), Xbox Series X/SPrice: $79 / £69 / AU$129Release date: November 19, 2026Genre: Open-world action-adventure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is easily the most impressive entry in the (in)famous series and a technical showcase that raises the bar for open-world games. Its expansive map and myriad activities offer countless hours of crime-fueled mayhem, while the intriguing characters keep you invested in the narrative. This game was worth the wait and will arguably go down as the finest title of this console generation.

Enormous, explorable open world.

Sources indicate that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Platforms: PS5 (reviewed), Xbox Series X/SPrice: $79 / £69 / AU$129Release date: November 19, 2026Genre: Open-world action-adventure.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is the most impressive video game I’ve ever played. I’m not surprised, given Rockstar Games’ history of releasing technically proficient (and insanely profitable) titles, but the storied developers have truly outdone most other games with what they’ve accomplished here. The long wait and anticipation are more than justified.

Larger than any locale in the franchise’s history, the fictional state of Leonida is a character unto itself, evoking real-life Florida with its myriad eccentric characters and diverse locations. You explore this vast landscape alongside the game’s two protagonists, a Bonnie-and-Clyde-like couple who help keep the emotional center in place amid the chaos of the main story and side quests. Together, the narrative and open-world elements deliver an experience that keeps you hooked for hours.

Sources indicate that I’ve been a huge fan of the GTA series since GTA 3 arrived in 2001 and completely changed the gaming landscape. I had some trepidation about GTA 6, given how long we’ve waited for it and how much gaming (and the world) has changed since GTA 5was released in 2013. Thankfully, GTA 6 far exceeds my expectations and will more than likely be my favorite game of the generation. Here’s why...

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 straddles the line between the more grounded tone of GTA 4 and the over-the-top insanity of GTA 5. It’s fair to say this game feels like Red Dead Redemption 2 set in the 21st century, in both tone and theme. Given that RDR 2 is in my top 10 favorite games of all time, this is a major bonus.

Industry observers note that that Red Dead inspiration is most evident in the game’s first chapter, where we slowly learn about the two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a criminal couple trying to build a latest life. The slower-burn intro will turn off anyone who's played the arcade-y GTA Online for the past 13 years—and it’s a valid criticism, even if I personally didn’t mind it. After chapter 1, it’s full-on GTA-style mayhem.

In a recent development, jason and Lucia have more grounded personalities than some of the wilder protagonists in older GTA titles, but the game generally does a good job of showing what motivates them and making you feel invested in their journey. Jason and Lucia balance each other, with the former more stoic and calculated and the latter more impulsive and instinctive. The characters are at their best together and feel incomplete apart. The leads’ relatively toned-down attitudes also contrast nicely with the absolutely bonkers characters they meet along the way.

Industry observers note that in true GTA fashion, this is a rags-to-riches criminal tale that builds with each subsequent mission. You feel the sense of progression as you move up in the world and take on bigger, more dangerous heists. Watching the protagonists evolve over the course of the story is also satisfying.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has been revealed that in the Grand Theft Auto series, driving has often been a point of contention, and that hasn’t changed here. At least initially. During the first few hours, I found the driving mechanics overly sensitive and loose. It felt like I was driving on ice, especially in the beat-up jalopy Jason owns at the beginning.

It has been revealed that then I realized that, at least on PS5, the triggers are pressure-sensitive, and I shouldn’t just hold R2 all the way down. In fact, you can feel a bit of resistance when you depress the button halfway. When I figured this out, I was golden. Though some vehicles naturally control better and differently than others, I now have a good handle (no pun intended) on the pretty intricate driving mechanics.

Pay & Spray shops are not only great for a quick paint job to lose the cops, but also for tuning your car’s performance for better handling. This can be expensive, so it’s best to wait until you have enough money and a car worth investing in, since you don’t want to upgrade a piece of crap. I like tuning cars because it reminds me of Rockstar’s Midnight Club racing series. And yes, you can totally add neon lights and nitrous!

Stealing cars is more involved than ever. While you can easily steal most cheaper or older cars, higher-end vehicles will have alarms, key fobs, and trackers. And even when you successfully jack a car, you need to hotwire it. The game doles out specific tools needed to steal various cars at specific points, so you'll need to be patient to grab the really high-end rides. Even if jacking cars requires more than a button press, the extra steps make stealing them feel more immersive.

As criminals, Jason and Lucia always end up getting into gunfights—either with fellow lawbreakers or law enforcement. Though the shooting and cover mechanics aren’t as precise and responsive as a dedicated third-person shooter like Gears of War: E-Day, they’re the most refined of any previous GTA game.

In a recent development, auto lock for weapons was essential in GTA 5 and RDR 2 because the free-aiming mechanics were so dodgy and imprecise. That’s not the case here, as I can easily land headshots with auto lock disabled. This game has its own version of Red Dead’s “Dead Eye,” called Focus Mode, which slows the world down so you can target specific body parts. This is crucial if you want to shoot arms or legs to disable rather than kill, especially since it ties into the game’s morality system. Jason and Lucia both have a Focus meter that drains while you’re in Focus Mode.

The cover mechanics are good but not great. I say that because while your character sticks to walls or the sides of cars you’re hiding behind, it’s too easy to snap out of cover when you try to move. Still, the mechanic works well enough most of the time, and you definitely want to stay in cover during intense shootouts with gang members or the police.

You have access to all manner of handguns, shotguns, assault rifles, and more, which you can purchase from Ammu-Nation, pilfer from dispatched enemies, or find in the open world. Like cars, you can modify weapons. Of course, buying upgrades that improve handling, extend magazine capacity, add scopes, and more can get expensive, but it’s well worth it given the number of insane shootouts you’ll encounter during the story or out in Leonidas.

Sticking up pawn shops and robbing banks has always been fun in GTA, but it’s even more enjoyable now with two protagonists. I never get tired of watching how shop owners and customers react when Jason and Lucia bust in with guns drawn. While one makes sure no one tries anything funny, the other threatens the clerk into emptying the register. Sometimes someone tries to be a hero and stop you, so you have to stay on your guard.

Sources indicate that that scenario is for small shops, but if you want to break into a bank, you’ll need to prepare. Scoping out a place, either from the inside or outside, to locate exits and where the goods are kept is crucial to pulling off a successful heist. And don’t forget to have a getaway vehicle nearby, as the cops will arrive rapidly if alarms are triggered (though you can always try to disable them).

Along the way, you’ll also discover or be told where gangs hang out or where other criminal activity occurs. These locations often have jewelry, drugs, or other contraband that you can then sell to a fence for a big haul. As with bank robberies, you’ll want to scope out a location to identify entry points and other opportunities to exploit.

Recent findings suggest that the wanted system is more intricate than before. Committing crimes in a specific area raises your wanted level by up to six stars, with each star bringing more heat from law enforcement. You can drive to another county to lose the heat, but the cops will remember your vehicle, face, hairstyle, clothing, and that there were two of you. To really lose the cops, you’ll need to change your clothes, repaint your car, or temporarily split up.

In a recent development, for example, I got a 4-star wanted rating after a robbery went wrong. I drove my car deep into the woods and got out, using the trees for cover to avoid being spotted by helicopters. After finding a truck depot, I broke into a truck using a slim jim carjacking tool and stayed in the truck without turning it on. The cops swarmed the area but didn’t find me because I was lying low. After a few minutes, they left, and I drove off to change clothes and switch vehicles. None of this was scripted.

Since this is a crime game, I’m glad Rockstar updated the wanted system to feel more realistic and give you the freedom to evade the fuzz in ways not available in previous titles.

Now, I won’t go into exhaustive detail about all the side activities available. Suffice it to say that if you need a break from your criminal pursuits, there is plenty to do. That said, I want to discuss some of my favorites.

Industry observers note that like in previous games, you can do side missions for some of the zany characters you meet. I enjoy these because they are small stories unto themselves, and also let you experience more of Leonidas’ environment and cultures. No spoilers here, but some of these side missions are completely bonkers, and sometimes quite literally out of this world.

This may sound weird, given how I neglect to do this in real life, but I’m obsessed with taking Jason and Lucia to the gym. And it’s not just because I want them to look buff and hot. For instance, lifting weights boosts your strength, making you a bit harder to kill and letting you punch enemies out more easily. Boosting your cardio lets you run and swim longer, while raising your Focus can extend your Focus Mode. You can also boost these stats by brawling, running, or eating, but I find hitting the gym more efficient and fun.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll also find several events that lead to missions not marked on the map. For example, you might return to your car only to find a random woman in the backseat asking for help retrieving her dog from a biker gang, or an influencer might decide to snap photos of herself with your fancy ride. This is why it pays to explore methodically, as surprises are literally around every corner.

It has been revealed that among other things, you can participate in street or boat races, get drunk and blow all your money at strip clubs, do some mud wrestling, or unwind by watching TV (the in-game TV shows are hilarious) or doomscrolling on your phone with your partner in bed after a long day of chaos. There is no shortage of interesting activities to partake in here.

Industry observers note that I say this without a hint of hyperbole, but GTA 6 is the most graphically impressive and detailed game I’ve ever seen. Rockstar’s proprietary RAGE Engine is in full effect, delivering awe-inspiring visuals that bring Leonida to life. Videos online can’t compare to the experience of playing GTA 6 firsthand.

Recent findings suggest that the map is immense. Even at full speed on the highway, it can take five or more minutes to reach a destination. And you won’t even mind, since everything you pass is so wonderfully rendered, from distant bridges to forests beneath thick, darkening clouds. I especially love driving through Vice City at night, as the metropolis’ gleaming buildings and neon-drenched streets are a sight to behold.

Since Leonida is essentially a miniature version of Florida, it has similar biomes. These include muggy swamps, dense woods, and the terrifying marvel of the Caribbean Sea. As in RDR 2, the world is filled with all manner of animals, from small rats to enormous sperm whales. You can easily spend hours exploring each locale, as long as you’re wary of hungry alligators or sharks.

Humans are as intricately detailed as the animals and environments. During my playthrough, I didn’t see a single NPC who resembled another. I’m also impressed that certain character types appear only in specific neighborhoods, which adds to the realism. You can spend all day people-gazing, as the fine folks of Leonidas always have something interesting to say. But as with exploring the wilds, keep a weapon handy for when someone inevitably tries to mug you.

It has been revealed that I played on a PS5 Pro, which, like all consoles that GTA 6 is available on, is capped at 30 frames per second. During my time, I never once saw the frame rate dip, even during intense shootouts or fast-moving chase sequences. Naturally, your experience may differ, even if you’re also playing on a PS5 Pro, but I never encountered performance problems. And though I wish we could have gotten at least 40 fps on the PS5 Pro, the locked 30 fps runs as smoothly as possible.

According to recent reports, beyond the gorgeous visuals, the GTA 6 experience isn’t complete without its incredible soundtrack. With over 22 radio stations featuring dozens of songs, there’s no shortage of awesome tracks to play while you commit crimes.

As before, you get a nice mix of stations featuring contemporary and classic tunes. There are also a handful of talk radio stations, which have always been a favorite of mine. Every station has an eclectic DJ or two to keep things lively. The radio stations also round out the world of GTA 6, offering entertaining insights on celebrities, famous establishments, current news, and more.

Recent findings suggest that the original tunes are just as nice as the expansive licensed soundtrack. You mostly hear this music during cinematic scenes, but it also pops up when you’re fleeing the cops. There’s also a particular track from rap duo Bau-Luxe that will have you laughing out loud because of its obscene lyrics that I won’t even hint at here!

This has been one of my longer game reviews, and even it only scratches the surface of the GTA 6 experience. Suffice it to say, you can (and some will) sink countless hours into this world and still not see everything Rockstar managed to cram into it. Like an expensive drink you can buy in Vice City, this is a title you’ll want to savor, not rush.

GTA 6 is everything we could have hoped for and more. Despite a few minor quibbles, nothing here detracts significantly. I’ve never given a game I’ve reviewed at Tom’s Guide a full five stars, but if any game deserves that honor, it’s certainly GTA 6. It’s a once-in-a-generation title that shows what’s possible when you give a talented team the budget and time to craft something exceptional. GTA 6 really is that damn good!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has announced that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The tech giant’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It noted that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The Newly introduced York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the tech giant’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

He won’t make that mistake again!

Industry observers note that despite putting the organization at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, mentioned that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones remarked: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the tech giant making the announcement in a press release.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” stated Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Firm. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

In a recent development, “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a newly introduced industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

In a recent development, as previously declared, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The tech giant’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

The show is also bucking the trend of big-ticket competition indicates moving out of Los Angeles by moving its second season to California, having shot the first season in Australia.

According to recent reports, deadline understands that the BBC Studios-produced show has been successful in its bid to receive the California tax credit. This would make it only the second unscripted show to receive the credit after Netflix’s upcoming series Schooled!, which comes from YouTuber Mark Rober and Jimmy Kimmel’s production tech giant Kimmelot. It would also become the first show to successfully score the tax credit in order to relocate to California, which was one of the core missions of the California Film & Television Jobs Act. Watch on Deadline.

It is a massive boon for the business in California, given that the pendulum has been swinging the other way recently with shows such as American Idol moving to Georgia and The Masked Singer moving to Upcoming Jersey.

The first season of The Next Pro employed around 110 local cast and crew and contributed an estimated A$7.2M ($5M) to the local Australian economy, per Screen Queensland.

The law, otherwise known as California Assembly Bill 1138, was signed in to law in 2025 by Gov. Gavin Newsom, expanding the tax credits system to include unscripted demonstrates for the first time. The act now covers “large-scale competition shows” with around 15% of its budget allocated to relocating television series.

The Next Pro will return next year for its second season. It will feature eight aspiring make dancers competing for the chance to become the next male pro on Dancing with the Stars, which is currently airing its finale episode.

The spinoff will join its mothership in California; Dancing with the Stars, which premiered in 2005, has filmed all 35 seasons of the show in Los Angeles.

Dancing with the Stars superfans will also have the chance to partner with hopeful contestants and help determine if they have what it takes to make it to the ballroom.

Robert Irwin returns as host, although, at the moment, it’s unclear if three-time Mirrorball champion Mark Ballas and his mother Shirley Ballas, who is the head judge on British OG format Strictly Come Dancing, will return as judges.

Dancing with the Stars: The Next Pro is produced by BBC Studios. Conrad Green serves as showrunner and executive produces alongside Deena Katz, Ryan O’Dowd, Krystal Whitney and Alex Cross are executive producers. Quinn Lipton is co-executive producer.

I used to take my AirPods Max with me on planes, but lately, I've been fine with just my Pros, since the noise cancellation seemingly blocks just about as much background sound as my over-the-ear headphones. Equally great are both the transparency modes, which pump in outside sounds while you're wearing your AirPods, and Adaptive Transparency, which automatically adjusts the level of transparency based on how loud or soft your surroundings are. This is a great mode for wearing your AirPods in loud environments, so you can still hear everything without the noise becoming overwhelming. To that point, these AirPods are actually FDA-certified hearing aids.

There are plenty of other features available here as well, especially if you have a compatible iPhone. AirPods Pro 3 have a built-in heart rate sensor, so you can track workouts without an Apple Watch; you can translate conversations in real time with Live Translate; "Conversation Awareness" lowers the volume of your audio and turns on transparency mode when you start speaking; and they run for eight hours on one charge with noise cancellation enabled.

  • Among Rosenberg’s first starry projects was Herbert Ross’ The Owl and the Pussycat in 1970.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, philip Rosenberg, the production designer who won an Oscar for his work on All That Jazz and also worked on films such as Network, Moonstruck and The Hurricane, has died. That, according to his nephew, Alan Rosenberg. No cause of death was given. He was 91.

Rosenberg was raised in Brooklyn before studying scenic design at Yale University with Donald Oenslager. About that time, he was hired as an assistant at the Metropolitan Opera where he worked with Ita Maximovna and Eugene Berman. His first film was The Seagull in 1968, on which he was a design assistant.

Among Rosenberg’s first starry projects was Herbert Ross’ The Owl and the Pussycat in 1970. Rosenberg was the art director on the film starring Barbra Streisand and George Segal. He transitioned to production designer on James Toback’s The Gambler before making a splash in 1976’s new Hollywood landmark Network, becoming known for the realism which made that period’s films stand out. Watch on Deadline.

After Network, Rosenberg would go on to work with direction Sidney Lumet on Daniel, Garbo Talks, Running on Empty and many more.

He likewise had a long-running working relationship with Norman Jewison. The two collaborated on Moonstruck, Other People’s Money, The January Man (which Jewison produced) and The Hurricane.

Rosenberg’s breakthrough came on All That Jazz in 1978. His work on Bob Fosse’s film earned him an Oscar, which he shared with Tony Walton, Edward Stewart and Gary J. Brink. He would be nominated again in 1978 as an art director on The Wiz.

Will Siri AI threaten Apple’s environmental target, given Google and Meta admissions?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (989 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials.
  • All of this could potentially be put at risk by the organization’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….
  • In a recent development, apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials. It has led the way with its use of renewable energy, made significant strides with carbon-neutral production, and removed plastic from all its packaging.

All of this could potentially be put at risk by the organization’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….

In a recent development, apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect. For example, when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 were carbon neutral back in 2023, that claim was described as “bogus,” with the EU banning Apple from repeating it. The company has also been criticized for pushing a relentless annual iPhone cycle, encouraging frequent upgrades.

Overall, however, Apple has first-rate credentials when it comes to the environment. It was way back in 2018 when the organization hit its goal of running its own operations off 100% renewable energy. This includes all Apple facilities, from Apple Park through data centers to its worldwide retail store network.

I stated at the time that using more environmentally friendly packaging should be the firm’s next priority, and it has indeed made great progress with this over the years, succeeding in removing all plastic packaging earlier this year.

After its own operations, Apple set about trying to tackle the power usage of its manufacturing partners. Back in 2020, the company set a goal of having its entire supply chain be carbon neutral by 2030. Just four years later, Apple mentioned it was 95% of the way there.

Sources indicate that the organization also helps fund and support a wide range of environmental initiatives around the world. Just a few examples include conservation in China’s national parks, environmental protection and carbon removal in Australia and Newly introduced Zealand, and helping to fund the build-out of renewable energy capacity in India.

Potentially, however, the vast energy demands of the data centers powering AI services could put its 2030 goal at risk. Other tech giants have already admitted that it may lead them to fail to hit their own renewable energy promises.

Back in 2024, for example, Google CEO Sundar Pichai stated that the AI boom was “challenging” to the manufacturer’s 2030 carbon-free goal. CNET reports that Meta is now also admitting that it may fail to hit the same target.

Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the organization is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline.”.

Notably, a lot of Siri’s most advanced AI capabilities are at the moment powered by Google’s Gemini models.

According to recent reports, at the same 2024 event where Google expressed doubts, Apple reiterated its commitment to its 2030 target. Then-CEO Tim Cook repeated this assurance later the same year, although admitted it would be challenging.

Industry observers note that more challenges, yes. But are we coming off the goal? No, definitely not. With more data centers, you use more renewable energy, and we’ve built that muscle now […] I feel very good about 2030.

In the firm’s most recent environmental progress report, it stated that it was was still using 100% renewable energy despite using over 2.5 billion kWh of electricity to power its data centers.

We’re proud that 100 percent of that electricity came from renewable sources including solar, wind, and low-impact hydropower. To cover our needs, we build our own renewable power projects and work with utilities to purchase clean energy from locally obtained resources. We’re staying at 100 percent even as Apple’s data center capacity continues to grow.

The same report stated the manufacturer had achieved zero water use for cooling at its latest data centers.

At our three newest data centers, we use high-efficiency air-cooled chillers instead of water-cooled systems, resulting in zero water use for cooling.

However, the greatest challenge for Apple lies ahead. The reason that Google and Meta are now backtracking on their promises is that both companies now have massive AI capabilities. As yet, Apple does not.

What happens as Apple expands Siri AI capabilities as usage increases, and as the firm moves into agentic AI features? Is it realistic for the company to maintain its 100% track record with vastly greater data center energy usage?

Greenpeace expressed its own doubts earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that “AI will be the defining test of Apple’s climate commitments,” spokesperson Avex Li claims. “To preserve Tim Cook’s environmental legacy, the tech giant will need to show that AI growth can be accommodated within its existing climate commitments through absolute emissions reductions, additional renewable energy investment, and longer-lasting products.”.

Apple did not respond directly but merely pointed to its past statements and most recent environmental progress report.

I don’t doubt the manufacturer’s desire to maintain its track record, but if Apple does join the likes of Google and Meta in becoming a major AI player, sticking to its 2030 timing is going to become increasingly difficult.

In a recent development, do you think Apple will succeed? Please share your thoughts in the comments.
