Why Black Friday Is the Perfect Time to Start a Gym Membership

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most people are probably waiting until Jan.
  • In a recent development, the week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit.
  • In a recent development, this week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a new air fryer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the latest year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

In a recent development, the week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on new tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

In a recent development, this week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a new air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for latest Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

Deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

It has been revealed that try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

Industry observers note that be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

Gyms also run sales around New Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

According to recent reports, that's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're fresh. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

From Black Friday to New Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K plan works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your Upcoming Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

It has been revealed that this is also the season when many workplaces and health intends wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some plans include gym memberships or discounts.

HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before New Year's resolution time arrives.

#96991. Industry News: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (877 w)

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it debuted in 2017.
  • It has been revealed that with iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch.
  • I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it debuted in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories.

It has been revealed that with iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the new GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 ($149, reg. $249) experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios.

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

It has been revealed that once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

It has been revealed that as a side note: Apple Watch has more accurate treadmill workout tracking as part of watchOS 27. GymKit remains the gold standard for accurate data, though.

GymKit also avoids two awkward gym habits. You don’t need to hold the treadmill’s metal heart-rate contacts while jogging. You also do not need to wear a Bluetooth heart-rate strap.

AirPods Pro 3 become the heart-rate source (and likely your podcast or music audio source as well). iPhone becomes the workout computer, which you can monitor during your workout. And the treadmill fills in the machine data while providing the surface for walking or running.

In a recent development, apple has been moving more fitness features onto iPhone for years. iOS first made the Fitness app useful without Apple Watch as Apple Fitness+ leaned into iPhone as an entry point. AirPods Pro 3 pushed that further as the first AirPods with heart-rate tracking, after Apple tested the idea with Powerbeats Pro 2.

According to recent reports, iOS 27 brings those pieces together. GymKit on iPhone shouldn’t replace Apple Watch for people who wear one every day. Instead, it’s a great backup when your Apple Watch is dead, charging, or left at home.

It also gives iPhone and AirPods consumers a taste of the Apple Watch experience, which could attract future Apple Watch customers.

It has been revealed that in testing with iOS 27 beta 1, my Exercise ring didn’t upgrade as I worked out without wearing Apple Watch. But after I put my watch back on, the Exercise ring caught up, and the workout appeared in Fitness with the right data.

My sample 16-minute treadmill walk showed 0.66 miles, 65 active calories, 97 total calories, 32 feet of elevation gain, and a 115 BPM average heart rate, just like if I’d worn an Apple Watch.

I had been getting the impression that gym equipment manufacturers had been abandoning GymKit support - if they ever had done so initially. I even got the impression that the majority of equipment in Apple's own onsite Gym at the Apple Park may not have supported it - at least originally.

According to recent reports, does Apple have a webpage listing compatible brands and models? Like they do/did for HomeKit.

What is other people perception? Any rowing machines that support it?

…checks - surprisingly it looks like Peloton do support it on their bikes.

If I tried to use GymKit on iPhone without AirPods, the iPhone disconnected when the workout started because it had no heart-rate source. If I tried to start GymKit from iPhone while wearing Apple Watch, iOS pointed me back to the Workout app on Apple Watch instead, though you can continue without using the watch.

AirPods heart-rate permission also matters. You can manage it in Settings under your AirPods settings and privacy options. I had turned it off, mostly as a theoretical battery-saving move, but this test convinced me to turn it back on. AirPods Pro 3 can also work with Apple Watch to provide the best available heart-rate data.

GymKit on iPhone is one of those iOS 27 features that sounds small until it solves a real problem. If Apple Watch is your default workout tracker, it probably stays that way.

But if your watch dies or you forget it at home, iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 can now log a treadmill workout with real heart-rate data and real treadmill metrics.

#96990. 12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1034 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • Industry observers note that you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • According to recent reports, if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

Industry observers note that you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

According to recent reports, if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Recent findings suggest that most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting latest movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

Go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

In a recent development, pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

In a recent development, hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

According to recent reports, use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should initiative ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you plan to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most important advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

#96987. Here in the World: Letters of Albert Camus, 1944–1959

Here in the World: Letters of Albert Camus, 1944–1959

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1320 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that what an amazing behemoth of a book!
  • On D-Day, Camus was thirty; Casarès was twenty-one.
  • According to recent reports, the correspondence was first published in French in 2017; now it has been (brilliantly) translated by Sandra Smith and Cory Stockwell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that what an amazing behemoth of a book! I’ve been lugging it around for weeks. Nearly a thousand letters: the intimate correspondence of Albert Camus and Maria Casarès. When they first met in Paris – on D-Day, 1944 – Camus had already published L’Etranger (1942; The Outsider). Born and raised in Algeria, he was in Paris when the Second World War broke out, and later joined the French Resistance. Camus’s wife, Francine Faure, a mathematician and pianist, remained in Algeria. Maria Casarès was originally from Galicia, the daughter of an exiled former prime minister of Spain, Santiago Casares Quiroga. In 1944, Casarès was already known as an actress, having played the titular role in J M Synge’s Deirdre of the Sorrows. She later starred in Les Enfants du paradis (1945), Cocteau’s Orphée (1950) and La Lectrice (1988), among other films and plays.

On D-Day, Camus was thirty; Casarès was twenty-one. They began an affair, but this ended when Camus was reunited with his wife. In 1945, Faure gave birth to twins: Catherine and Jean. In June 1948, Camus and Casarès met again and embarked on a long relationship, which continued until Camus’s death in a car crash on 4 January 1960. Afterwards, the poet René Char found Casarès’s letters in Camus’s apartment and discreetly returned them to her. In the 1990s, not long before she died, Casarès offered the letters to Camus’s daughter, Catherine.

According to recent reports, the correspondence was first published in French in 2017; now it has been (brilliantly) translated by Sandra Smith and Cory Stockwell. The letters are passionate, voluminous, at times torrential. Everything is discussed: love, sex, books, plays, films, beauty, art, family, madness, fear of failure, fear of death. Also logistics, travel intends, inadequate postal services, money troubles, indigestion, hives, headaches.

Recent findings suggest that in her preface, Catherine Camus writes: ‘Their letters make the earth more vast, space more luminous, the air lighter, simply because they existed.’ Casarès, she believes, is ‘like the ocean: breaking, crashing, re-forming and starting over again with stupefying vitality’. Camus is pretty oceanic as well. Both lovers travelled extensively; the letters are often scrawled in haste, sent from Paris, Cabris, Oran, from North and South America, written on ocean liners, or ended abruptly to catch the post. Sometimes, too, they are written as a sort of diary, across several days. The tempo changes. There are lists, schedules; they want to know what the other has been doing, hour by hour. How many glasses of wine they’ve drunk. What they’ve eaten. Who they’ve seen. There are ecstatic protestations of love. And questions, lots of questions. What happened last night? Are you happy? Did you see a doctor? They both emerge vividly – fascinating, erudite, witty, anxious; flawed and paradoxical.

It has been revealed that as Catherine Camus says, there is great luminosity; many descriptions of humid summer nights, bright oceans, shimmering mountains. Also, a rich sense of being finite and alive, briefly here in the world: ‘I didn’t sleep any better last night, and tonight it’s so hot, there are so many crickets and stars that I have no hope of falling asleep. At least I can write to you…’ (Camus). Or, ‘Today the sky, which was a drab deep gray this morning, gradually brightened up, and around 2:00, you could just about see the sun peeking through a soft veil’ (Casarès). They struggle with grief, sorrow and anxiety, with physical asperities. Camus endures savage bouts of TB, ‘getting undressed again, letting myself be poked and prodded’. For a while, Francine Faure is depressed, consigned to a hospital, repeating the name ‘Maria Casarès’. Camus and Casarès agonise about her. Sometimes, they argue furiously: ‘You’re stupid, my poor darling!’ writes Casarès, ‘and we must wait for it to pass!’ The war has ended, cities lie in ruins, everything feels untethered and surreal: ‘Of course, the world is still sick, even if I’m well,’ writes Camus. ‘Will we always have to love each other during the Apocalypse, in anguish, in torment?’.

Often, they discuss books and authors. They’re not fans of Hemingway. On reading To Have and Have Not (1937), Casarès writes: ‘I certainly found some well-written pages but, my God, how dusty, dull, gloomy it all is, and it smells so much of rooms with peeling wall­paper, all of them a mess, with the odor of sheets, night sweats and dirty clothes!’ Camus’s response is yet more scathing: ‘Hemingway? It serves you right! Why read phonies with no talent?’ Proust gets a mixed review: Casarès is ‘hooked’, loves the way he writes about nature, but finds the ‘political gossip’ boring. In January 1950, Camus sends ‘bad news’:.

George Orwell died. You don’t know him. A very talented English writer, who had the same experience as me, more or less (even though he’s ten years older), and exactly the same ideas. He’d been fighting tuberculosis for years. He was one of a very small number of men with whom I shared something.

Both Camus and Orwell opposed the adamantine absolutes of communism and fascism; both were attacked for their political views. They had arranged to see each other in Paris in 1945, but Camus was afflicted by another bout of TB and the meeting never happened. A few months after Orwell’s death, Camus gives a copy of Nineteen Eighty-Four to Casarès. She isn’t convinced: ‘I didn’t learn anything from it that I hadn’t already imagined, and it left a weak impression on me.’.

In a recent development, when it comes to his own books, Camus is full of self-doubt, grappling with his ‘tormented, mistrustful soul’. He works ‘like a madman’ on L’Homme revolté (1951; The Rebel), but fears it is a failure: ‘I only hope that this book won’t be too far from what it was meant to be. I hope it will help people to live – that it will say that all is not lost – that it will give everyone with whom I feel solidarity the strength to hate nothing, and to create.’ Even after receiving the Nobel Prize in 1957, Camus is still ‘trying to find some equilibrium within myself’. As for Casarès, in one of the last letters she describes herself as ‘here, a little shapeless, it’s true – a little like you, perhaps, or like the world that surrounds us – but I’m here nonetheless, whole and alive’. It’s impossible to know if they wrote with any sense of eventual publication in mind, or simply and entirely for each other. Camus usually drafted and redrafted his published works. Even his Notebooks were edited – by Camus himself, and by Francine Faure, among others. In the end, these letters are so surreally intimate, so poetic and unbridled, that it feels a bit like reading an extraordinary epistolary novel: about love, art, war, finitude and crazy-­beautiful optimism. All is not lost indeed.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely newly introduced side of the game.

If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

According to recent reports, hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

Recent findings suggest that when you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

In a recent development, while driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

It has been revealed that when you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

Jenna Ushkowitz doesn’t want to remember when Glee did a tribute to Cory Monteith after his death.

In a fresh interview, the star of the musical comedy explains why it was difficult to film the episode and why she felt they shouldn’t have done it.

“To shoot ‘The Quarterback’ [tribute episode]… I think it wasn’t the right thing,” Ushkowitz remarked on the We Need to Talk podcast. “And I think everybody collectively agrees that it’s maybe not the thing that we should have done, because we were grieving both privately and publicly.” Related Stories News Jane Lynch On 'Glee' Reboot & If She'd Return: "I Would Love To Do Sue Sylvester For The Rest Of My Life" News 'Glee' Stars Stage Broadway Mini-Reunion As Hulu Reboot Gears Up.

Monteith played Finn Hudson in the Ryan Murphy series until his death in July 2013. The show continued and paid tribute with an episode dedicated to the late actor, which also acknowledged that the quarterback from the fictional William McKinley High School had died. Watch on Deadline.

Recent findings suggest that “I think the fans definitely needed something, because they loved Cory so dearly like we did, and [loved] Finn so dearly,” Ushkowitz remarked. “But it’s a really hard thing to be grieving your friend and be a character grieving their friend at the same time.”.

According to recent reports, she continued, “It was like, too soon for that. [It] was not fun, [I] don’t want to remember that time. The show itself was never the same. He knew everybody’s names. He just was such a good person, a kind person.”.

Ushkowitz mentioned that at the time “even our creators, they were dealing with grief too” and “nobody had the tools” to deal with Monteith’s death.

AI May Be Scanning Your Private Signal Chats

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads.
  • In a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy.
  • Recent findings suggest that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

In a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy. Systems-level capabilities like Gemini Intelligence (on Android) and Siri AI's Onscreen Awareness (on iOS and macOS) scan your screen and may be able to capture data from Signal conversations in the process, which can then be used to perform tasks. Not only does this potentially expose your information, but that of other conversation participants as well. Whitaker notes that this leaves privacy protections outside of Signal's control because the platform cannot easily restrict AI access to the app.

Recent findings suggest that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

The main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

Consumers on iOS 27 can confirm or manually disable screenshot protection via Settings > Privacy > Block Siri AI. The compromise with this setting is that it also blocks you from taking screenshots of Signal conversations in the app and App Switcher, though you can disable it temporarily for 10 minutes if needed. On Android, Signal automatically engages the "Screen security" setting when it detects an AI agent attempting to access the screen. This, too, blocks screenshots inside the app and can be disabled via Settings > Privacy > App security > Screen security. Signal cannot block screenshots on macOS 27. However, users can add Signal to their Excluded Apps list via System Settings > Siri, which at least limits proactive access to conversations by Siri AI.

#96971. Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1481 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if you or someone on your shopping list wants a newly introduced smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from.
  • There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark.
  • Sources indicate that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you or someone on your shopping list wants a newly introduced smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

Luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Sources indicate that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own organization, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

Industry observers note that the Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

Where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

Industry observers note that you also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

Sources indicate that for an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

As a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET says Android users can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

It has been revealed that based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

Industry observers note that while the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android customers, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

It has been revealed that the Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

According to recent reports, in CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

Industry observers note that CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?).

CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.).

Industry observers note that in CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

In a recent development, still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another tech giant drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.

iOS 27 gave your iPhone an alarm feature that’s long been missing

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (391 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alarms are one of the most notable iPhone features, and iOS 27 offers a key feature that should help your alarm actually wake you: a new volume setting for alarms that’s independent of other volume settings.
  • According to recent reports, have you ever accidentally slept through an alarm?
  • I suspect that’s a pretty common reason for missed alarms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alarms are one of the most notable iPhone features, and iOS 27 offers a key feature that should help your alarm actually wake you: a new volume setting for alarms that’s independent of other volume settings.

According to recent reports, have you ever accidentally slept through an alarm? We’ve all done it. And most often for me, it’s because my alarm volume was unintentionally set to a very low level.

I suspect that’s a pretty common reason for missed alarms. And in iOS 27, Apple finally has the fix—but it requires manually setting up.

Inside Settings ⇾ Sounds & Haptics, you can now set a volume for alarms that’s independent from the systemwide ringtone setting.

iOS 27 has two fresh sections in this Settings screen: Alarms and Timers, and Alerts and System Sounds. Both include ‘Match Ringtone Volume’ toggles that are on by default. This means your volume for alarms, timers, alerts, and other system sounds are all determined by the ringtone volume.

But if you disable the Alarms and Timers toggle, you’ll get a upcoming volume slider that applies only to those system functions, and won’t be impacted by your ringtone volume.

As seen above, this means you can crank the Alarms and Timers volume up to the maximum level without making every other system sound, including notifications and phone calls, be similarly deafening.

So the next time you sleep through your alarm, it won’t be because the alarm was too quiet.

In case you missed it, iOS 26 introduced a welcome feature that lets you set custom snooze durations for alarms, and also an option to have alarms trigger on your iPhone even if you’re wearing an Apple Watch.

Do you blueprint to set a custom volume setting for alarms in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

EXCLUSIVE: Ahead of the finale of hit K-drama The Remarried Empress, Korean actress Shin Mina, who plays Empress Navier in the show, talked to Deadline about her experiences of playing the role and shared her thoughts on why the show is such a huge success.

She also shared some tips on what viewers could look out for in the final two episodes, which are dropping on Disney+ and Hulu later today (November 25).

Sources indicate that also starring Ju Jihoon, Lee Jongsuk and Lee Seyoung, The Remarried Empress has been a breakout hit in Korea and internationally, becoming the most viewed local original premiere of all time on Disney+ globally, just three days after its launch on November 3. Related Stories News Black Friday Streaming Deals Offered By Disney+, HBO Max, Paramount+, Peacock & More Casting Kelly Rowland Joins Hulu's 'Reasonable Doubt' For Season 5.

It has been revealed that premiere views increased worldwide around 40% between its first and second weeks of streaming, with Latin America leading as the fastest-growing region, with views increasing by 43%, followed by APAC and EMEA at 39% and the U.S. at 37%. Watch on Deadline.

Based on a Naver webtoon, the story revolves around Empress Navier and her dignified response when her husband, Emperor Sovieshu of the Eastern Kingdom, takes a slave girl as a concubine and suggests marrying her. While keeping her composure, Navier becomes closer to Crown Prince Heinrey, who can take the form of a magical bird. At the end of episode eight, we saw Navier inform her husband that would she accompany the Prince to the Western Kingdom to attend his coronation as king following his father’s death.

This was Shin’s first time playing an Empress in a romantasy epic, although she found some common ground with characters she’s played before: “I’ve appeared in a period drama before, Arang And The Magistrate, a fantasy-infused historical series, but I played a ghost in that one, so it was a very different experience from a traditional historical drama,” she tells Deadline.

“This time, even though the setting is an imaginary era, playing a character with a symbolic status in a world with social classes felt newly introduced to me. Above all, I loved that Navier’s dignity, strength, and wisdom are at the heart of the story. And I thought she was an incredibly proactive and appealing character, since in the end she chooses to remarry on her own terms.”.

Shin admits she also got a kick out of wearing so many different styles of dresses. While Korean period dramas are usually filmed in traditional Hanbok, The Remarried Empress uses European-style costumes and sets and was filmed in castles and palaces in Germany and the Czech Republic.

“I wore so many dresses and tried so many different hairstyles. I kept thinking, ‘when will I ever get to film in dresses this gorgeous again?’ so I enjoyed every moment while acting. Of course, the costumes weren’t always comfortable,” Shin laughs.

Industry observers note that but while she plays an Empress in a fantasy setting in the series, Shin claims Navier is not so different to characters she’s played before: “There are seeds of love in Navier’s heart, too. As they slowly sprout, she realizes how she truly feels and chooses a upcoming love. I think those emotional shifts, and the moments of facing love, connect with the characters in other romance projects I’ve played.”.

On the huge success of the show, Shin says the popularity of the original webtoon meant that audiences around the world were looking forward to the adaptation, but that also put a lot of pressure on the cast and crew. “We knew many people were looking forward to the drama, but I’m sure some were also worried about a live-action adaptation,” Shin says. “So I was really curious how this newly introduced challenge would be received.

“When we started filming, I was worried about whether I could rapidly immerse myself in this unfamiliar setting. But after shooting a few episodes, those concerns disappeared naturally. At some point, I was completely focused on the story unfolding within that world.

“Just as the cast did, viewers got immersed in this world and its characters faster than I expected, which was surprising and made me very grateful. I never imagined the drama would be loved this much.”.

Sources indicate that she says that, in particular, fans are cheering on the character of Empress Navier. “I think people relate to the situation Navier is in. She may look strong and cold on the outside, but she cares deeply for her people and indicates warmth toward the imperial maids and Queen. I’m grateful that viewers understand and empathize not only with her human side, but also with the responsibility of living as the perfect empress and the pressure that comes with it.”.

Recent findings suggest that shin adds that she enjoyed filming in Europe, and that shooting in real castles helped her get into character: “Being able to film in places steeped in another country’s culture and history felt very fresh to me. Wearing gorgeous dresses and filming in such exotic locations actually helped me become even more immersed in the world of the series.”.

Recent findings suggest that as for tonight’s finale, Shin doesn’t want to drop any spoilers, but has this to say: “I hope viewers will watch the finale wondering what the Eastern Empire will look like without Empress Navier. I also hope you’ll cheer on Navier’s future after making a upcoming choice, the future of the Western Kingdom, and the future she will build together with Heinrey.

In a recent development, “Navier has always lived with genuine care for the Eastern Empire and its people. So I’d love for viewers to pay attention to what she feels as she leaves her homeland and chooses a latest life, and to the emotions of someone standing at the start of a new beginning.”.

In addition to Arang And The Magistrate, Shin’s previous credits also include My Girlfriend Is A Gumiho (2010), Oh My Venus (2015), Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha (2021), Our Blues (2022) and No Gain No Love (2024).

Produced by Studio N, The Remarried Empress is directed by Cho Suwon and adapted for screen by Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol. Ju Jihoon plays Emperor Sovieshu, with Lee Jongsuk playing Crown Prince Heinrey and Lee Seyoung as the slave girl Rashta.

Industry observers note that we first got a glimpse of how big the show would become at this year’s Busan International Film Festival, which premiered the first three episodes to packed theaters. So far the producers are keeping mum on whether there will be a second season, but that looks like something the fans are hoping for.

The final two episodes are dropping today at 5:00pm KST, 4:00pm HKT, 8:00am GMT and midnight PST.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales.
  • Industry observers note that while BNPL aims can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any major discounts.
  • In a recent development, to be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the company is not uniquely misleading on this front.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales. As you're adding item after item to your cart during the sale, you might be tempted by offers for an "affordable monthly payment system." Also known as "buy now, pay later" (BNPL), the pitch is a tempting one: Buy what you need now, and pay later, "on your own timeline." But as convenient as it sounds, you should think twice before using buy now, pay later options, whether during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, or at any other time.

Industry observers note that while BNPL aims can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any major discounts. Let's take a look at the hidden costs of BNPL, and why you're better off paying upfront for all your Black Friday purchases.

In a recent development, to be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the company is not uniquely misleading on this front. The process is straightforward: you choose your items, select Affirm (a third-party lender) at checkout, complete a quick application, and receive an instant decision on your loan terms. Individual transactions initiated through Affirm are limited to $25,000, with a daily maximum of $100,000 across multiple purchases—but of course, your Black Friday splurge will be nowhere near that major, right? (Right?!).

In a recent development, the main draw of these programs is the ability to "pay at your own pace." If you are required to pay a down payment, that is due at the time of the transaction. From there, your first monthly payment is usually due one month after your purchase is processed. Each following payment will be due one month later, on the same day of the month.

Sources indicate that you can choose your own timeline, usually spanning 3, 6, 12, or 24 months, depending on the purchase amount and your creditworthiness. Unlike traditional credit cards, Affirm shows you the exact payment amount and total cost upfront, and claims no hidden fees or compound interest.

According to recent reports, you need a separate Affirm account in addition to your Amazon Prime membership. The application process requires basic information, including your name, mobile phone number, date of birth, and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Affirm performs a soft credit check initially, which doesn't impact your credit score, though they may conduct a hard inquiry for some loans.

BNPL plans are helpful if you really need to finance something big, but whenever possible, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses.

The ease of this sort of financing can make expensive purchases feel more affordable than they actually are. When you can buy a $1,000 tablet for "just $67 per month," it's easy to lose sight of the total cost, as well as your overall financial picture. In turn, this makes it all too easy to overspend on items you might not have purchased otherwise. You're better off taking a breath, stepping away from your shopping cart, and setting alerts to be notified when a product hits a price you can stomach, at a time you can afford it.

According to recent reports, despite what you may have heard in the past, BNPL providers may report to credit bureaus, meaning your BNPL purchases can in fact affect your credit score. For instance, all Affirm payments (including on-time, late, and missed payments) are now reported to the credit bureau Experian. So if you miss payments or default on the installment plan, it will cause damage to your credit score—making it even harder to get approved for mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and other financing down the road.

Still, not all BNPL providers report to credit bureaus or use the same type of credit check, so it’s key to understand the specific terms and practices of any service you’re considering.

Sources indicate that when you use a credit card, you get valuable purchase protections like extended warranty coverage, price protection, and the ability to dispute fraudulent charges. BNPL plans generally don't come with these safeguards. This means you're on the hook if something goes wrong with your BNPL purchase and the retailer doesn't make things right. The smarter move is to only buy what you can afford during a sale, no matter how tempting those deals may seem.

Although installment plans are helpful if you really need to finance something major, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses. Better to wait for a good price for something you truly need and can afford to pay for right now.

If there's a massive-ticket item on sale for Black Friday but it's still out of your budget, consider these two questions before you turn to BNPL through Affirm:.

Industry observers note that is this really an essential purchase? BNPL should really only be used on completely necessary purchases that you can’t afford right now, but can afford in six weeks. On that note...

In a recent development, will I be able to pay this off within six weeks? When a bigger payment gets broken down into smaller installments, you might find yourself overspending in the long run, because it "feels" like you can afford it. Stay on top of how much you’re actually spending—especially if you're considering multiple BNPL purchases—and how it will impact your overall budget going forward.

For more information about deals and discounts, keep an eye on all of Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Sources indicate that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (715 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest glitch with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat.
  • MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.
  • Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest glitch with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge. Anker’s answer in the MagGo 2 Pro is a small fan inside of it. Anker claims it keeps the charging surface below 96.8°F, and the fan adjusts its speed based on what’s plugged in and how the charge is progressing. You can switch between Cool and Silent modes if you don’t want to hear it running at all.

According to recent reports, the result of having this fan is a Qi2.2 power bank that actually reaches Qi2.2 speeds for a full charge. Anker rates it at 25% on an iPhone 17 Pro in 10 minutes, then to 50% in 25 minutes, which is the kind of speed you’d normally expect from a wired charging session.

The MagGo 2 Pro battery is 10,000mAh, which is enough for a little over one full charge of an iPhone Pro Max and closer to two on a standard iPhone. Size-wise, it has about the same footprint as the iPhone itself and is roughly an ounce lighter than Anker’s standard MagGo. It’s not a slim battery, but for one with a fan, it’s workable in your travel bag, crossbody, etc.

Sources indicate that the single USB-C port works both directions at up to 45 watts. If you plug in a 45-watt charger to it, the MagGo 2 Pro can charge from empty to 80% in under an hour. The same port will charge a Mac or an iPad up to 45 watts in a pinch, which is a nice add-on for a MagSafe battery. You are not going to charge up your MacBook Pro from zero to full with it, but it’s a nice way to get a little charge in an emergency at the airport, etc.

One thing to know before you buy: the cable in the box is a 1-foot USB-C-to-USB-C cable, and Anker indicates that reaching the full 45-watt recharge speed requires a 45-watt-rated cable. So keep that in mind as you pack for a trip.

Recent findings suggest that anker put a small display on the side that cycles through six screens with a side button: charging wattage, battery percentage, battery health, and temperature. It’s a nice touch to know you are reaching the 25-watt Qi 2.2 speed.

There’s also a built-in stand that adjusts from flat to 80 degrees and folds back into the body when you’re done. You can also swiftly turn off charging if you simply want to use it as a stand. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro comes in Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, and Starlight Silver.

Qi2.2 is the Holy Grail of MagSafe chargers, but as I stated in the beginning, it’s irrelevant if the heat throttles it. To get full 25-watt MagSafe charging on the go, you’ll likely need something with a fan, unless you’re in colder weather. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro solves that problem with a built-in fan, a handy side display, and a stand.

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is available on Amazon and directly from Anker.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that black Friday isn't until Nov.
  • Sources indicate that millions of Amazon Prime users right now pay $14.99 per month or $139 per year for their memberships—though other plans cost less if you qualify.
  • If you’re on the fence about signing up for (or renewing) your Prime membership, here’s how to judge whether or not the benefits outweigh the $139 cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that black Friday isn't until Nov. 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sales have been ramping up for several days. For frequent Amazon shoppers, Prime can swiftly pay for itself—mostly thanks to the free shipping perk. But how does the math shake out if you aren't regularly ordering from Amazon? Is it worth signing up if you only shop during major sales?

Sources indicate that millions of Amazon Prime users right now pay $14.99 per month or $139 per year for their memberships—though other plans cost less if you qualify. For example, the Amazon Prime Student program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

If you’re on the fence about signing up for (or renewing) your Prime membership, here’s how to judge whether or not the benefits outweigh the $139 cost.

Here are the main perks of Amazon Prime that make it worth the cost for so many people.

It has been revealed that free two-day shipping on millions of items: This is the main draw of Prime. If you shop frequently on Amazon and want quick free delivery, the shipping perks alone may make Prime worthwhile. Prime members also get free same-day delivery on over 3 million items in eligible areas. The ultra-fast (and morally suspect) shipping usually costs $9.99 per order for non-members, though you can choose lower-cost or free shipping options if you're willing to place larger orders and wait longer to receive them.

In a recent development, access to Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals. If you ask me, the content library isn’t as robust as Netflix or Hulu, but this is still an added value.

Other Prime benefits: You also get Amazon Music for streaming songs, Prime Reading for ebooks, magazines, and audiobooks; Prime gaming, free photo storage, and occasional exclusive discounts/deals.

Sources indicate that amazon Prime Rewards Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon/Whole Foods purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the annual fee.

Number of users: Prime benefits can be shared with other members of your household. The more users, the more value per person.

Let's say you don't care about Prime Video, Amazon Music, or free e-books, and just want to know if you'll save money you would otherwise be spending on shipping.

For non-Prime members, Amazon requires a minimum order of $35 to qualify for free shipping on eligible items. The average shipping costs for non-members aren't publicly listed, and can vary by item and shipping speed, typically ranging from $5 to $10.

It has been revealed that for our purposes, I messed around on my non-shared, non-Prime Amazon account to find an average shipping cost of around $6 per order (assuming the order total fell below the $35 threshold, of course). Of course, shipping costs will vary depending on the item and how quickly you want it, but let’s compare the cost to the appeal of Prime’s two-day shipping option. So, we have the cost of individual online orders (around six bucks) compared to the free delivery that comes with an $139 annual fee. This means the costs you’d save on shipping alone make Prime worth the cost as long as you place more than two dozen orders in a year.

In other words: The $139 annual fee pays for itself as long as you order from Amazon Prime at least twice a month.

Of course, this conclusion is strictly in terms of shipping costs. How it stacks up ethically is between you and the person in the mirror.

And then there's this important caveat: You can still get free shipping from Amazon without a Prime membership, provided your order has $35 or more of eligible items. However, this won't grant you Prime shipping speed—your order will typically take five to eight days to be delivered. But you can place fewer, larger orders and wait a little longer, and still never pay for shipping.

Also worth considering is how much of that membership cost you'll be able to recoup via exclusive Prime Day offers. During the sale, some items will be heavily discounted only for Prime members—but whether the Prime Day price is really a "deal" will vary greatly based on the item you're buying. Some of those "substantial discounts" aren't any greater than what the item typically sells for. The Prime Day price can even be higher than other sale prices throughout the year. That's why it's important to make sure what you're ordering is something you planned to buy anyway—and that the sale price is actually a true bargain—before you order.

In a recent development, the cost of a Prime membership is a solid value for anyone using Amazon 23 times per year or more—especially if you're also watching highlights on Prime Video or purchasing something that is deeply discounted for Prime Day. But if you only shop on Amazon a few times a year and don't take advantage of Prime Day offers or the other benefits, then that $139 annual fee isn't necessarily paying for itself.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

I Tried Building My Own Interactive World in Google Genie, but Real-Time AI Engines Aren't There Yet

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (987 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Beyond the Gemini assistant, Gemini Notebook, and various other AI offerings, Google also develops Genie, a world-building engine intended to help you create immersive visual experiences and games using only text prompts.
  • These promises point to the future of AI in all kinds of ways—from robotics to world sims—but the tool requires a lot of computing power, and access is limited for the time being.
  • It has been revealed that it's no exaggeration to say you can build an entire virtual world in Google Genie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beyond the Gemini assistant, Gemini Notebook, and various other AI offerings, Google also develops Genie, a world-building engine intended to help you create immersive visual experiences and games using only text prompts. Think of them like AI videos you can interact with and move through.

These promises point to the future of AI in all kinds of ways—from robotics to world sims—but the tool requires a lot of computing power, and access is limited for the time being. You can dive in now if you're on one of the Google AI Ultra plans ($99.99 or $199.99 a month), or join the waitlist if you're a Google AI Pro user ($19.99 a month). But if you've got access, is it worth the effort (and money)? I put it to the test.

It has been revealed that it's no exaggeration to say you can build an entire virtual world in Google Genie. It's going to be a more basic, less developed, and more chaotic world than the one in, say, GTA 6, but you can do it. Think of it like generating an AI video from a prompt, but you can then walk through the video and go as deep as you like, taking turns along the way.

Everything is rendered in real time, at a resolution of 720p and at 24 frames per second. That's not to say the engine is storing a massive 3D map in memory, however—after a minute or so, it's going to start to forget the places you've already seen. And while the basic layout will stay fixed, you might notice disappearing trees or changing colors.

Google's official line is "visual details and object permanence can still shift or drift over time" in Genie 4, so it's a known limitation. The tool is presented as-is, with the intention to develop it further over time as models improve, and it's aimed at filmmakers, historians, designers, scientists, robotics engineers, and game developers. Or indeed, anyone who just wants to get lost in a world that isn't real.

According to recent reports, some of the demos you'll find as you step through the Genie 4 portal give you a great idea of the possibilities. There's a "Dino Field Guide" that, you guessed it, lets you wander safari-style through a prehistoric habitat. All the flora and fauna are neatly rendered, and you even get dinosaur quiz questions along the way—a nod to Genie's potential as an educational tool.

According to recent reports, there's a "Villa Giallo" mini-game, which involves searching a haunted 1970s Italian villa and clicking on objects as you go; these objects act as clues to help you progress to the next room. I was also intrigued by a "White House: Code Red" experience that takes you into the West Wing during a "high-stakes national crisis." I couldn't quite figure out what the crisis was, but I definitely felt the highness of the stakes.

Recent findings suggest that someone's even built a "GTA 7" engine that drops you into a bright and vibrant cityscape. The slow speed and warped physics of the experience suggest Rockstar Games has nothing to worry about just yet—check out the disappearing cars and backwards-driving cops in the video above—but it's impressively detailed all the same, considering it all comes from a few text prompts.

In a recent development, having checked out a few demos, I felt ready to put Genie 4 to the test myself. Eager not to infringe on any IP, I decided to generate a world where I wouldn't mind getting lost for a few minutes—somewhere I could get away from the stress of my day and enjoy some warmer weather.

I started with the prompt "Create a fully immersive, photorealistic 3D environment showing a pub in an English village in the middle of a hot and sunny day. The pub is surrounded by country lanes, old buildings, and woods, and a handful of villagers are walking around and drinking outside the pub. Use a first-person view and use a quiet background of birdsong and wind rustling in the trees.".

It took a couple of minutes for my peaceful, idyllic world to be ready, and then I was immediately able to navigate through it using my keyboard and mouse. Once you're in your world, you are suggested certain prompts you can make use of, like strolling into the pub or getting the villagers to make a toast, and these worked well—evidence that your virtual world really is interactive (to a point).

Unsurprisingly, the usual AI video tells are in abundance: Everyone looks generic, the physics often go sideways, the text on signs is gibberish, and details don't remain fixed. Do a full 360-degree spin around, and you might find that not only have all the customers in the pub changed their appearance, but you're also at an entirely different pub.

It has been revealed that the best feature is the ability to make real-time edits: I summoned both a storm and a cricket pitch with a few text prompts, though Genie decided to put a hut in the middle of the cricket pitch for some reason. I think I was most impressed by the moment when a cricketer walked past me and commented on the rain, providing hints of how this kind of tech could expand or augment games and virtual experiences in the future.

In a recent development, that said, even at v4 of Genie, this tech is still very much in the experimental stage, and while I can see the potential, it also reveals just how difficult a task world-building is for an AI engine. Without 3D maps and proper physics engines as a foundation, you'll encounter a great deal of hastily rendered slop as you explore your environment. Even if you're a prompting pro, for the time being this is something to mess around with, rather than use in a practical way.
